Answer: B
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 1a) clearly demonstrates a hyperdense linear foreign body (fishbone) penetrating the esophageal wall with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating esophageal perforation. In the context of circulatory collapse and this imaging finding, pneumothorax (or pneumomediastinum leading to tension physiology) is the most likely directly observable complication resulting from the breach of the aerodigestive tract into the mediastinum/pleural space.
